memos.headline: AAPL and JPM Lead Near Highs; MSFT and XOM Show Persistent Relative Weakness
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. AAPL at 315.32 is just 0.3% off its 52-week high with +13.1% 12-week relative strength vs SPY and RSI at a healthy 62.9—this is the cleanest uptrend in the group. JPM and UNH are similarly positioned near highs with strong 4-week momentum, though UNH's +25.1% premium to its 200-day mean makes me cautious about chasing. On the other side, MSFT sits 29% off its 52-week high and 12.9% below its 200-day average—a confirmed downtrend I want no part of until it reclaims at least the 200-day. XOM is printing -15.7% 12-week relative strength vs SPY with RSI at 44.3 and nearly 19% off highs, another name to avoid. CAT's 66% 26-week return is extraordinary but the 5% ATR and 10.6% drawdown from highs suggest the easy money is behind us and risk/reward is less compelling here.

views.note: Trading 0.3% from 52w high, +5.9% above 50d, RSI 62.9 not yet overbought—trend is pristine; would reassess on a close below the 50-day (~298).
Near 52w high with +8.8% 4w return, +6.8% above 50d, low 2.03% ATR—strong trend with contained volatility; invalidated below 310.
Massive +26.4% 12w relative strength and only 1.6% from highs, but +25.1% above 200d mean raises mean-reversion risk; would trim on a break below 400.
Down 29% from 52w high, 12.9% below 200d mean, negative relative strength on every timeframe—clear downtrend; need a sustained close above 430 to reconsider.
RSI 44.3, -19% drawdown, worst 12w relative strength in the universe at -15.7% vs SPY—broken trend; would need a close above 150 to revisit.
Positive 26w return and above 200d, but 12w relative strength vs SPY is flat at -1.4% and RSI is middling at 57—no edge either way until it clears 235 or breaks 195.
Sitting 3.4% below 50d mean with -10.2% 12w relative strength vs SPY and RSI at 50.9—directionless; need a move above 260 for conviction.
Stunning +66.3% 26w return but 5% ATR is the highest in the group and it's 10.6% off highs with RSI cooling to 49.8—momentum fading, risk elevated; watching 900 as support.
Above 200d by 12% but slipping below 50d by 4.2% with RSI at 47—intermediate trend intact but short-term softening; would get interested on a reclaim of 370.
Flat to slightly below 200d mean, -12.1% drawdown, negative relative strength on all timeframes—no reason to own from a trend perspective.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Post Extraordinary Earnings Growth; XOM and UNH Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I am most convicted on the names showing durable, high-margin earnings acceleration and most cautious where net income is contracting on flat revenue. NVDA's 2027Q1 quarter is staggering: $81.6B revenue (+85% YoY), $58.3B net income (+211% YoY), a 71.5% net margin, and only $8.5B total debt—this is the cleanest earnings profile in the universe. GOOGL delivered $110B revenue (+22% YoY) with net income surging 81% to $62.6B and a 57% net margin on just $14.8B debt, suggesting operating leverage is still expanding. On the other side, XOM's net income collapsed 46% YoY to $4.2B on essentially flat revenue (+2.4%), compressing net margin to 4.9%—a commodity-price problem I cannot underwrite. UNH grew revenue only 2% to $111.7B with net income flat at $6.3B and a thin 5.6% margin against $77.9B debt; any further medical-cost pressure would erode earnings power. I would revisit XOM if net margin recovers above 8% and UNH if revenue growth re-accelerates above 5%.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, net margin 71.5%, net income +211% YoY on minimal debt of $8.5B—unmatched earnings power in the universe.
Net income +81% YoY to $62.6B with 57% net margin and low $14.8B debt signals durable operating leverage.
Revenue +18% YoY, net income +23% YoY, 38% net margin, and manageable $40B debt make this a high-quality compounder.
Net income surged 77% YoY to $30.3B and margin expanded to 16.7%, though $122.6B total debt warrants monitoring.
Solid +17% revenue growth and 26.6% margin, but $82.7B debt and slower earnings growth (+19%) versus peers temper enthusiasm.
Revenue +22% and net income +27% are strong, but 14.6% margin and $36.2B debt against $17.4B quarterly revenue leave limited margin of safety in a cyclical downturn.
Steady 10% revenue growth and 33% net margin are respectable for a bank, but $449B total debt and cycle sensitivity keep me neutral.
Defensive 18.5% margin and 7% revenue growth are fine but unexciting; I need to see margin expansion above 20% to get constructive.
Net income down 46% YoY to $4.2B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin signals commodity-driven cash-flow compression I cannot underwrite.
Flat net income (-0.2% YoY) on only 2% revenue growth with $77.9B debt and 5.6% margin points to earnings stagnation.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% but Sticky 4.2% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Squeeze Duration and Favor Defensives
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode—the upper bound has been flat at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the prior year, and the June effective rate of 3.63% confirms no movement. The problem is inflation: the CPI index rose 2.0% over just the last three months (roughly 8% annualized) and is up 4.2% year-over-year, which makes further easing very unlikely near-term. The 10-year yield has climbed 25 bps in three months to 4.56%, while the 10y-2y spread has compressed 13 bps to +0.38 pp, signaling the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.20%, down 10 bps over three months, so there is no recession catalyst to force the Fed's hand. A material downside surprise in the next CPI print or a jump in unemployment above 4.4% would change my regime call from 'hawkish pause' to 'easing imminent,' but until then I favor sectors that benefit from or tolerate higher rates and avoid long-duration growth names most sensitive to discount-rate pressure.

views.note: Banks benefit from a hawkish-pause regime with a positively sloped curve at +38 bps and stable employment supporting credit quality.
Energy acts as a natural inflation hedge; with CPI running 4.2% YoY and no easing in sight, real-asset exposure is attractive.
Staples offer defensive positioning but pricing power may be tested if sticky inflation compresses margins; hold but don't add.
Cyclicals face cross-currents: stable employment supports capex but rising long rates and a flattening curve historically cap multiples.
Long-duration growth is most vulnerable as the 10-year yield rises to 4.56% and the Fed shows no inclination to ease further.
High-multiple tech faces discount-rate headwinds with 10y yields up 25 bps in three months and no near-term rate relief.
Quality growth with recurring revenue offers some buffer, but rising long rates cap upside; I stay neutral until the rate trajectory clarifies.
Consumer discretionary plus long-duration profile is a tough combination when CPI is running hot and the 10-year is at 4.56%.
Ad revenue cyclicality is offset by strong cash generation; macro headwinds keep me from going long but fundamentals prevent an avoid.
Healthcare is a classic late-cycle defensive with pricing power that can pass through inflation; stable labor market supports enrollment.

memos.headline: Limited Sentiment Signal Across Universe; XOM and GOOGL Show Elevated Corporate Activity Worth Monitoring
memos.body: I am working with an unusually thin sentiment dataset this cycle—only 8-K filings with no GDELT tone or volume data to parse, so my conviction is low across the board. NVDA's Q1 earnings 8-K on 2026-05-20 drew a -1.8% next-day price reaction, and subsequent board-level changes (7/2) suggest the narrative may still be digesting mixed results rather than turning positive. GOOGL stands out for sheer filing density: five 8-Ks in three weeks spanning material agreements, bylaw amendments, and officer changes, which in my experience signals a corporate restructuring narrative that media will amplify—direction unclear, so I stay neutral. XOM's massive 2026-07-01 8-K covering an acquisition completion, delisting notice, bylaw changes, and officer moves is the single most event-rich filing in the set and could drive a sentiment shift once media coverage catches up. AMZN's 2026-06-10 material agreement creating a direct financial obligation followed by two 'Other Events' filings suggests a capital-raising or deal narrative building quietly, which I read as mildly constructive if tone turns positive.

views.note: Post-earnings -1.8% reaction and subsequent board turnover suggest sentiment has not yet found a floor; waiting for tone inflection.
Five 8-Ks in three weeks including material agreements and officer changes create noise that could swing either way; no clear directional tone signal yet.
The dense 2026-07-01 8-K covering acquisition completion and structural changes is likely under-covered by media so far, creating a potential positive sentiment catalyst as coverage builds.
Material agreement and new financial obligation on 6/10 followed by two Other Events filings suggest a constructive deal narrative forming ahead of broader media pickup.
Six filings over five weeks are routine for a bank of JPM's size; Reg FD and officer changes are standard and unlikely to shift media tone materially.
Single officer departure/appointment 8-K provides almost no sentiment signal; insufficient evidence to take a directional view.

memos.headline: Falling Oil and Compressed VIX Suggest Geopolitical Risk Premium Is Fading, but Policy Uncertainty Remains Elevated
memos.body: I see a mixed geopolitical backdrop as of July 10. WTI crude has collapsed 26.6% over three months to $73.15/bbl, signaling either demand destruction or easing supply-side tensions—either way the energy security premium has meaningfully deflated. VIX at 15.84 (down ~20% over one month) and HY OAS tightening to 2.70% both indicate markets are not pricing acute geopolitical disruption, yet the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index remains elevated at 282.56 and ticked up 2% month-over-month, which I read as lingering concern around trade/export-control policy rather than kinetic conflict. Without concrete new sanctions or export-control escalations in the 8-K filings I have for NVDA, GOOGL, or AMZN, I treat the current environment as structurally benign but with a policy tail risk that would crystallize if new China semiconductor restrictions or tariff actions are announced. A reversal in oil above $85 or a spike in the EPU index above 350 would change my view materially.

views.note: No new export-control escalation visible in the June 8-K, but NVDA remains the highest-beta name to any China semiconductor policy shift, keeping me sidelined until clarity improves.
WTI down 26.6% in three months to $73.15 signals fading geopolitical supply premium; unless OPEC or sanctions dynamics tighten supply, energy earnings face headwinds.
Policy uncertainty is elevated but not worsening on a 3-month basis, and GOOGL's recent 8-K filings show no adverse regulatory or geopolitical disclosures; I lean constructive at current risk levels.
CAT's Reg FD disclosure in June and the still-elevated EPU index suggest management is navigating trade-policy uncertainty; I stay neutral until tariff or infrastructure-spending direction clarifies.
Tightening HY spreads and a positive yield curve at +38bp support bank earnings, and multiple routine 8-Ks show no geopolitical stress in capital markets operations.
Two recent 8-Ks lack detail on supply-chain or trade-policy impacts; with EPU still above 280 and potential tariff risk to e-commerce logistics, I hold neutral pending more information.
